scope: Read-only product diagnosis from observed synthetic deck and exact current source; nonauthor context reuse disclosed.

findings.observed: Actual v3 failed Deck CI badge leads to Trace saying current validation passed and publish ready.
findings.cause: NodeSlideStudio queries evaluateLatest; InspectorPanel passes Deck CI only to AiInspector and routes its click to Trace. Trace receives workspace.validations without Deck CI. ValidationSummary promotes that narrower publishOk field to an unqualified readiness phrase.

exactBlocker.message: The final materialized deck repeats composition geometry: Slides 3 and 4 are near-duplicates (similarity: 0.98)

findings.smallestRepair: Pass the existing current Deck CI receipt/loading state to Trace; show the actual blocker and affected slide positions beside explicitly scoped structural validation. Reserve overall readiness language for a current, matching full gate result. Keep fail/loading/unavailable distinct; do not suppress or lower the diversity gate.

findings.observed: The explicit illustrative 100/120/140 chart request becomes a generic six-slide deck with no chart in either canonical JSON or actual PPTX.
findings.cause: Landing inserts generic purpose/audience; deterministicBriefSpec prefers purpose for opening and closing and emits a fixed narrative scaffold. Primitive generation recognizes special metric CSV/top-scorer phrases, not the supplied prose sequence. Deterministic creation skips the provider critique report.
findings.smallestRepair: Preserve the original unmet prose request and disclose the currently recognized data shape. The real CSV-append attempt also failed at normalization; repair that separate prompt seam before another UI/export proof. Do not invent NLP chart parsing or auto-dispatch a provider.

findings.observed: The exact supported CSV was submitted through the actual landing UI, but its five line breaks were flattened and the actual persisted deck/PPTX still contained zero charts.
findings.cause: validateNodeSlideCreateDeckFields sends prompt through the common single-line boundedCreateText helper, which collapses all whitespace. nodeslideAgent consumes that returned brief before deterministic generation. The line-oriented CSV parser consequently finds no standalone header.
findings.smallestRepair: Treat only brief.prompt as bounded multiline content. Preserve internal whitespace and Unicode, normalize CRLF/CR to LF if that is the declared contract, trim only outer whitespace, reject blank-only input, retain raw 4000-code-point and 8192-byte ceilings and all other field normalization. Do not split/reconstruct CSV in downstream renderers or add a chart-specific regex exception.

contract.title: nonempty, maximum 180 characters/540 UTF-8 bytes, unique case-insensitive
contract.content: normalized nonempty text, per-file 24000 UTF-8 bytes; at most 3 attachments/60000 total bytes

supportedInput.replayScope: Original pure plan retained; new offline materializer cause proof is supplemental. Real CSV-append creation failed. Attachment UI path remains untested.

nextProof: Freeze both actual failing journeys and current source before editing.

Verify LF/CRLF/CR, internal spacing/Unicode, blank input and raw character/byte overlimits through actual validator and deterministic materialization; include exact old-normalizer knockout.

Through ordinary owned local UI, resubmit the exact original brief plus CSV, reload and export; independently verify canonical chart and actual PPTX chart values, labels and current notes. Keep original prose-only request unmet.

limitations: No new browser, backend request, provider/model call, dependency install, application build, native Office call, or candidate source/index/ref mutation. Only existing pure modules were compiled in memory for offline evaluation.

The offline Deck CI replay uses the exported v3 snapshot and exact current evaluator bytes. It is not a captured Convex response; agreement with the displayed count/status and deterministic evaluateLatest source supports the causal attribution.

Original CSV parser result was a planned spec only. A later separate pure materializer replay proves chart survival only for intact multiline input and the attachment path; the actual CSV-append UI journey failed. Neither pure result proves a repaired persisted/exported chart.

Metric CSV primitive parsing uses the first literal metric,value,unit,source header, at most the following 100 lines, simple comma splitting and first eight finite numeric rows for generic charts; it is not a general RFC CSV parser. The generic chart unit is value; source-column text is not consumed by this parser.
The original natural-language chart request remains unmet. CSV is an explicitly different supported input and does not retroactively satisfy the original request.
Root owns concurrent responsive first-use evidence. Current notes-control overlap and doubled-content clipping are separate recorded observations, not evaluated or graded here.
No full readiness, human usage, native PowerPoint compatibility, deployment, production quality, or 44-criterion score is inferred. Full grades stay null and the 4.5 target stays unchanged.

Reviewer context is reused across portfolio slices; this reviewer did not author NodeSlide product changes. Earlier failed read probes were missing guessed file paths only; no product command or test failure was hidden.

Root real CSV-append counterexample supersedes any implication that pure parser support is already usable through the landing textarea. The original pure receipt is retained without promoting it to a user-journey pass.
